shortDesc.message: Tab audio booster (up to 600%). Optional Turbo: EQ, toolbar boost & higher cap; checkout in the extension when you upgrade.

storeDesc.message:
🎧 600% Sound Volume Booster — clearer, louder audio for Chrome tabs

Turn up quiet videos, music, calls, and streams without fighting the system volume. The extension is built around one goal: make what you are already watching or listening to easier to hear.

🔊 Basic mode

Raise playback up to about 600% with a simple popup, per-tab controls, saved levels per site, keyboard shortcuts, and a light or dark theme. Pick up where you left off on each site without redoing the same tweak every time.

🖥️ Fullscreen mode — a standout for movies & shows

Fullscreen is where many of us actually watch: films, series, live streams, and long YouTube sessions. This extension is designed to work well in that flow — your boost stays with the tab that is playing, so comfortable levels carry over while the player fills the screen. Handy on laptops, hotel Wi‑Fi, or any setup where built‑in speakers feel too soft under fullscreen video.

⚡ Turbo mode (optional)

Same extension, extra headroom when you want it: roughly 800% cap, one-click reapply from the toolbar when a tab is playing audio, and EQ shaping (bass, mid, treble) with presets to tame harsh peaks on big boosts. Trials or subscriptions are optional; account sign-in and checkout run inside the extension only if you choose to enable or purchase Turbo. Standard boosting does not require Turbo.

🎬 Typical use

Open a tab with sound, click the extension icon, adjust the level. Works across common media and streaming sites. Increase gradually and use levels that stay kind to your hearing and your hardware.

❓ Questions

Q: Is a paid subscription required?
A: Core tab boosting works without a paid plan. Turbo is optional; paid or trial access is handled in the extension through the billing partner if you upgrade.

Q: Does it work with headphones?
A: Yes. The extension changes how loud the tab sounds on your device.

Q: Is it safe for speakers and headphones?
A: Very high levels can stress drivers or hearing. Increase gradually and follow equipment guidance.

🔒 Privacy

The core volume feature processes audio in the browser as described in the extension privacy notice; it does not upload your tab audio to our servers for that purpose.
